# Mentoring a new engineer toward small pull requests

Situation: A junior engineer joined my team straight out of school. She was technically strong
but quiet in design reviews, and held pull requests back until they were perfect, so they were
huge and slow to review.

Task: Help her get feedback earlier and speak up in design discussions.

Action: We agreed she would open a draft pull request within a day of starting any task, even a
skeleton, and before each design review she wrote down one question or concern ahead of time so
she had something ready to say. I reviewed her drafts the same day so the habit paid off quickly.

Result: Within a few months her pull requests were small and frequent, and by the end of the year
she was leading the design of a service on her own. She now teaches the draft-PR habit to new
hires.
